subject: OB
stem: 24-year-old, 8 weeks amenorrhoea, RIF pain + vaginal spotting, pyrexial, cervical excitation on bimanual. Most likely?
options: B. Ectopic pregnancy – ruptured/unstable must be excluded urgently
explanation: Demo recall: pain + bleeding + amenorrhoea + peritonism/cervical excitation = ectopic until proven otherwise. Resuscitate, beta-hCG, TVUS, surgery (laparoscopy/laparotomy by stability).

subject: OB
stem: 33-year-old sudden severe colicky RIF pain radiating to back/pelvis, vomiting, tender mobile RIF mass. Most likely emergency?
explanation: Sudden unilateral severe pain + vomiting + adnexal mass = torsion. Doppler US, urgent gynaecology – detorsion/oophoropexy, ovary often salvageable early.

subject: OB
stem: 32-year-old multigravida, 32 weeks, sudden painless pool of blood at night, now stopped, transverse lie, maternal pulse 120, BP 110/70, FH 145. Most likely?
explanation: Painless third-trimester bleeding + malpresentation = praevia. No PV exam; resuscitate, Rh status, steroids if preterm, US placenta location, C-section if major.

subject: OB
stem: 26 weeks: BP 165/110, proteinuria 2+, headache, hyperreflexia. Diagnosis and seizure prophylaxis?
options: B. Preeclampsia with severe features – magnesium sulfate + timely delivery
explanation: Preeclampsia: HTN + proteinuria/end-organ after 20w. MgSO4 prevents eclampsia; delivery is definitive. Control BP urgently.

subject: OB
options: B. Magnesium sulfate IV loading + maintenance
explanation: Eclampsia: MgSO4 is drug of choice; secure airway, control BP, deliver when stable.

subject: OB
stem: Multiparous woman just delivered: boggy uterus, heavy vaginal bleeding. First steps?
options: A. Uterine massage + oxytocin + fundal assessment + resuscitation
explanation: Atonic PPH: call for help, massage, oxytocin, empty bladder, check placenta/trauma, tranexamic acid early, transfuse if needed.

subject: OB
stem: 28 weeks PPROM: pooling, ferning positive. Afebrile, fetus cephalic, no labour. Management?
options: B. Expectant + steroids + antibiotics (erythromycin) + monitoring, no digital PV unless in labour
D. Induction at all gestations immediately
E. Bed rest with no steroids
explanation: PPROM preterm: prolong latency if no infection/distress – steroids for lungs, antibiotics, surveillance. Avoid digital exams.

subject: OB
stem: 28-year-old heavy prolonged periods, pelvic pressure, enlarged uterus with firm mass. Most likely?
explanation: Menorrhagia + bulk symptoms + firm uterine mass = fibroid. US confirms; manage by symptoms/fertility (tranexamic, hormonal, myomectomy/hysterectomy).

subject: OB
stem: 22-year-old severe dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia, chocolate cyst on US. Most likely?
explanation: Cyclic pain + infertility + endometrioma = endometriosis. Laparoscopy gold standard; COCP/progestin/GnRH + surgery per severity.

subject: OB
stem: 24-year-old oligomenorrhoea, hirsutism, acne, BMI 32, polycystic ovaries. First-line?
options: B. Lifestyle weight loss + combined OCP for cycle/hirsutism; metformin if dysglycaemia
explanation: PCOS: lifestyle is foundation; COCP regulates cycles/androgens; manage fertility with letrozole/clomiphene when desired.

subject: OB

explanation: HPV testing is primary screen in most UAE-aligned guidelines; follow abnormal with colposcopy/biopsy.

subject: OB
stem: 35-year-old smoker, migraine with aura, wants contraception. Safest?
options: B. Copper IUD (or progestin-only if suitable) – avoid oestrogen with aura/smoking>35
explanation: Migraine with aura + smoking >35 = oestrogen contraindicated (stroke). Copper IUD highly effective, no hormones.

subject: OB
stem: Middle-aged woman post ovarian cancer: menarche 17, COCP 5 years, multiparous. What increases endometrial cancer risk?
options: B. Unopposed oestrogen exposure (e.g. theca-cell tumour, obesity)
D. Smoking – protective but never recommended
explanation: Recall: COCP, late menarche and multiparity protect; smoking is never advised. Unopposed oestrogen (obesity, theca-cell tumour, tamoxifen) raises risk.

subject: OB
options: B. Urgent endometrial sampling (pipelle/hysteroscopy + biopsy) + TVUS
explanation: Postmenopausal bleeding = endometrial cancer until proven otherwise. Biopsy + imaging promptly.

subject: OB
stem: New immigrant delivers baby with cataracts, deafness, microcephaly, hepatosplenomegaly. No drugs. Prevention for next pregnancy?
options: B. Rubella vaccination before conception (avoid in pregnancy)
explanation: Congenital rubella triad. Prevent by pre-conception MMR/rubella immunity check; vaccinate when not pregnant.

subject: OB
stem: Couple worried about Down syndrome. Definitive test and timing?
options: A. Amniocentesis ~15–16 weeks (or CVS 10–13w) for karyotype
explanation: Recall: amnio 15–16w definitive; CVS earlier. Screening (NT + biochemistry/NIPT) is not diagnostic.

subject: OB
stem: 38 weeks: diazepam, indomethacin, MgSO4, pethidine given. FHR 190→150 reactive. Which drug least likely to drop FHR?
explanation: Recall logic: opioids, benzodiazepines and MgSO4 all blunt variability and rate; indomethacin has the least direct fetal cardiac effect here. NSAIDs still need ductus and fluid monitoring.

subject: OB
stem: Pregnant woman with diarrhoea, Giardia confirmed. Safe treatment?
explanation: Recall: paromomycin is luminal, minimally absorbed – preferred for giardia in pregnancy per many sources. Avoid teratogens; consult OB/ID.
